exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Infant fecal vitamin K profiles (phylloquinone and menaquinones)
cohort: 46 mother-infant dyads (23 breastfeeding and 23 formula-feeding; 26 vaginal deliveries and 20 cesarean sections)
finding: Both feeding practice and delivery mode influence bacterial vitamin K production in the infant gut.
mod_finding: Total fecal menaquinones were greater in vaginally delivered infants compared to infants delivered by cesarean section.
